newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds slow pre-weekend, quiet week in prospect.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds slow pre-weekend, quiet week in prospect.

text.p: 1315 GMT -- Primary market activity was predictably light on Friday ahead of the weekend, with the wait for U.S. GDP data also having a dampening effect.
** New issue business next week will be hit by a triple whammy from the U.S. -- its FOMC meeting, monthly jobs report and July 4 holiday.
** Among today's deals, BNG asked for $200 million over two years at a two b.p. spread.
** The EBRD and World Bank both tapped the rand sector, with a zero coupon at 20 years and a 15.00 pct one-year deal.
** Xerox raised its exchangeable bond to $250 million.
The Eurobond market was quiet on Friday, ahead of the weekend and with the wait for final first quarter U.S. GDP data also a calming influence, syndicate managers said.
New issue business next week will be hit by a triple whammy from the U.S. -- its FOMC meeting starting Monday, the monthly jobs report on Thursday and July 4 holiday.
One likely deal was Croatia's debut mark Eurobond, now expected to be for up to 500 million marks at 85-100 basis points over German government paper, dealers said.
Among today's deals, Bank Nederlandse Gemeenten emerged with a straightforward retail-targeted deal, asking for $200 million over two years at a two b.p. spread.
Goldman Sachs International was lead manager. Paper was quoted at a bid spread of two b.p. on broker screens during the afternoon session.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development and World Bank both tapped the rand sector, with a zero coupon at 20 years and a 15.00 pct one-year deal.
The EBRD deal, led by Morgan Stanley, was a 1.0 billion rand reopening, reoffered at 8.05 percent, of an outstanding issue and brought the total nominal size to 5.5 billion rand.
EBRD paper was quoted on broker screens at 7.90 bid, a discount to the 8.30 issue price equal to the 0.40 point fees.
The World Bank transaction was for 1.0 billion rand jointly lead managed by Credito Italiano and Toronto-Dominion.
Elsewhere, the exchangeable bond launched by Xerox Credit on Wednesday was increased by $50 million to $250 million by lead manager UBS. The notes are exchangeable into Xerox Corp shares.
The coupon was set at 2.875 percent, the middle of the indicated 2.75-3.00 percent range.
